Adani Power.summary:
Effectively a one-house live view. **Jefferies** (May-2026, Buy, PT ₹255) is the only fresh, substantive call — built on capacity nearly doubling to ~31 GW and free cash flow turning positive by FY30E. **Asit C Mehta**'s positive note is a year old (May-2025) and thematic. There is no current bear in the captured set, which is itself worth flagging: a thinly-covered, recently re-rated Adani name with only one major house actively publishing is a thin base of consensus to lean on.

My own read: Adani Power is a genuinely different business from the one the market feared in 2023. The shift to ~95% PPA-tied capacity converts it from a merchant-price punt into something closer to a contracted utility, and pre-ordering equipment for the 23.7 GW pipeline (L&T/BHEL) is a real speed-to-market edge in a power-short market — that bull case is largely sound. What I'd weigh against it: (i) **group-level risk** — Adani-complex financing access, related-party scrutiny and sentiment can move this equity independently of plant economics, and broker operating models don't capture that; (ii) the **merchant / data-centre upside** the bulls love is the cyclical, least-reliable leg — fine as optionality, dangerous as a base case; (iii) **execution** — a ~23% EBITDA CAGR needs every GW commissioned on time with PLFs and coal supply holding. Net: I'd treat ₹255 as a credible *operational* target but discount it for the governance tail and the thin coverage. The real signposts to watch are coal availability, FGD-compliance capex (due Dec-2026), and fresh PPA wins.

Jeff|260518.change: Maintained Buy; PT held at ₹255. Thesis recentred on FCF turning positive by FY30E and falling leverage.
Jeff|260518.view:
Jefferies has the analytically strongest version of the bull case — it anchors on the de-risking (PPA cover up from ~80% to 95%) rather than just the capacity headline, which is the right emphasis: locked tariffs are what justify a utility-like multiple. The ₹255 PT at 20x EV/EBITDA, a ~100% premium to NTPC's implied 10x, is defensible if you believe APL's ~2.3x EBITDA growth through FY30E versus NTPC's ~1.5x.

Where I'd push back: 20x on a thermal generator — even a fast-growing one — bakes in a great deal, and a single covering house means no triangulation on those estimates. I'd want a second top-tier broker corroborating the FY30E numbers before treating this as consensus rather than one (good) analyst's model.

Asit|250521.change: Dated May-2025 thematic note — nothing recent to compare against.
Asit|250521.view: A year-old thematic piece; I'd disregard it for any current decision. Its main signal is the absence of deep, active sell-side coverage on the name right now.

AIA Engineering.summary:
Three houses cover AIA Engineering, split 2-bull vs 1-bear. **ICICI Direct** (Buy, PT ₹5,285) just upgraded from Hold following the 4QFY26 results beat — a sharp 31% PT lift from ₹4,035 in February. **Asit C Mehta** (Buy, PT ₹5,106) has been bullish since Sep-2024 on the high-chrome media conversion story, but that note is nearly 21 months old and carries limited fresh weight. **Nomura** (Reduce, PT ₹3,568) is the lone bear and the most recent local report: despite acknowledging a 21% EBITDA beat and 2% volume growth, they maintain a Reduce at a target roughly 14% below the ₹4,143 closing price, citing persistent uncertainties. The target spread is wide — ₹3,568 to ₹5,285 — reflecting genuine disagreement on whether the structural conversion narrative justifies a premium multiple when mining volumes still declined 4% y-y in the latest quarter.

My own read: AIA Engineering has a genuinely defensible niche — producing high-chrome grinding media for mining (gold, copper, iron ore) where it displaces lower-quality forged-steel media with demonstrably better wear rates. The conversion opportunity is real and long-cycle. But the stock's persistent premium valuation means any volume softness or delay in new mining-client ramp-up gets punished. Nomura's skepticism is the more intellectually honest of the current views: a 21% EBITDA beat didn't move their call, which suggests the bear case is about sustained earnings power, not a single quarter. ICICI's upgrade feels reactive — a momentum move on a results beat rather than a revised thesis. The two things I'd watch most: (1) whether global mining capex (especially copper and gold, where conversion is deepest) holds up through H2 CY2026, and (2) whether the next 1–2 quarters sustain cement-segment volume growth (15% y-y in 4Q) as a structural offset to lumpy mining cycles. If mining volumes stay soft while cement holds, the bull case weakens but doesn't break; if both soften, Nomura's ₹3,568 looks prescient.

Nomura|260527.change: PT maintained ₹3,568; Reduce maintained. No change from prior — both prevTP and currTP are ₹3,568, both calls REDUCE.
Nomura|260527.view:
Nomura is the useful contrarian here. Maintaining a Reduce at ₹3,568 — roughly 14% below the ₹4,143 CMP — even after a 21% EBITDA beat and a volume upside signals that their concern is structural, not cyclical: the stock is simply too expensive on normalized earnings. The note title ('uncertainties remain') reinforces this — they're not disputing the quarter, they're disputing the multiple.

This is the view I'd take most seriously as a check on bull optimism. AIA's premium is predicated on a long conversion runway that is real but slow-moving; if interest rates stay elevated globally and mining capex gets deferred, the re-rating could stall while the sell-side waits for 'next year.' Nomura is essentially saying the market is discounting several years of perfect execution and the risk-reward is poor. That's a coherent, hard-to-dismiss position.

ICICI|260527.change: Upgraded to Buy from Hold; PT raised ₹4,035→₹5,285 (prior Trendlyne entry: Hold at ₹4,035, 01-Feb-2026). No pdfdata match in local library — change derived from Trendlyne history.
ICICI|260527.view:
ICICI's upgrade on results day is textbook momentum: a strong 4Q beat triggers a rating flip and a 31% PT hike. That's not necessarily wrong — sometimes results clarity genuinely changes the risk-reward — but the timing and magnitude suggest the prior Hold was too cautious rather than the current Buy being deeply considered.

The ₹5,285 PT implies roughly 28% upside from ₹4,143 CMP and lands above even Asit's older ₹5,106 target. Worth noting that ICICI was at Hold/₹4,035 as recently as February — less than four months ago — and the business hasn't structurally changed, just delivered one strong quarter. I'd treat the upgrade as a sentiment signal rather than a new fundamental read. The PT is plausible if the conversion story re-accelerates, but ICICI hasn't published in the local library so the detailed reasoning isn't available to verify.

Asit|240905.change: Dated Sep-2024; no prior Asit report in the library to compare. Trendlyne shows Buy at PT ₹5,106 as of 05-Sep-2024 — the only Asit entry on record.
Asit|240905.view:
This is a stale 21-month-old note and should be weighted accordingly. The core thesis — high-chrome media conversion opportunity — remains the structural narrative that all bulls cite, but a lot has happened since Sep-2024: multiple quarterly cycles, a post-results ICICI downgrade to Hold in Feb-2026 (reversing the prior bullish consensus), and now an upgrade again. Asit's ₹5,106 PT happens to be close to where ICICI now sits, but the convergence is coincidental — not an updated view.

I wouldn't place much weight on this note in isolation. The conviction it expresses is the right long-term framing, but for near-term positioning the Nomura and ICICI notes (both 27-May-2026) are far more current and directly reflect the latest results.

Apollo Hospitals.summary:
A converged, recently-upgraded bull book. The three freshest houses all RAISED targets on the strong 4QFY26 — **Jefferies** ₹9,250→₹9,700, **Kotak** ₹8,980→₹9,520, **CLSA** to ₹9,280 — clustering tightly ~₹9,300–9,700, with **Prabhudas Lilladhar** also Buy. The only cautious note, **ICICI Securities** ('soft quarter; bed addition critical', Nov-2025), pre-dates the beat, and the older Geojit / ICICI Direct targets (₹7,763–8,840) have been outrun by the stock. So there is no live bear — the disagreement is about degree, not direction.

My own read: Apollo is the highest-quality way to own India's hospital structural story — an under-bedded market, rising insurance penetration, and a brand strong enough to push ARPOB through price and case-mix. The operating metrics (~68% occupancy, ~25%+ mature-hospital margins, ROCE rising ~16%→21-22%) genuinely justify a premium. But I'd surface the risks the sell-side is glossing over. **Valuation** is the big one: at ~27-33x EV/EBITDA the stock already prices near-flawless execution, so incremental upside leans on the HealthCo listing crystallising value rather than on the hospitals (which are excellent but largely in the price). **Regulatory price caps** are the under-weighted tail — NPPA/CGHS caps already trimmed oncology ~100bps and could broaden; a pricing-led margin story is exposed there. And the **~1,400-bed ramp** carries real execution risk (clinician hiring, payer onboarding) that could keep new-unit losses elevated past guidance. Net: constructive on the business, cautious on the entry multiple — a 'great company, demanding price' situation. I'd watch HealthCo listing progress and any widening of price caps most.

CLSA|260522.change: Maintained Outperform; PT ₹9,280 after the 4QFY26 beat.
CLSA|260522.view: An incremental post-results raise, in line with the pack — confirms the direction without adding a distinct angle.

Kotak|260522.change: Maintained Buy; PT raised ₹8,980→₹9,520 on rapid bed additions and better HealthCo/diagnostics margins.
Kotak|260522.view: The most balanced of the bulls — it raised the PT on genuine earnings drivers (bed adds + AHLL/diagnostics margins) while staying explicitly cautious on Apollo 24/7, which mirrors my own concern. If I had to anchor on one house here, it's Kotak.

PL|260522.change: Q4FY26 update; Buy retained (PT not parsed).

Jeff|260521.change: Maintained Buy; PT raised ₹9,250→₹9,700; FY27-28 EBITDA estimates +5%.
Jeff|260521.view: Jefferies sits at the top of the PT range and leans hardest on the HealthCo value-unlock. The call on hospital execution is excellent, but I'd treat the HealthCo / 24/7 leg as optionality, not banked — digital breakeven has been guided and slipped before, and a listing's value depends on a market window. Strong on the core, a touch generous on the catalyst.

MO|260211.change: Feb-2026 note (pre-4QFY26); bullish on hospital optimisation + HealthCo traction.
MO|260211.view: Directionally right but stale — superseded by the post-Q4 upgrades above.

Geojit|251219.change: Dec-2025: upgraded to Buy, PT ₹7,763 — now well below the stock; dated.
Geojit|251219.view: The level is overtaken by events; the early Buy call was correct, the target is now irrelevant.

ICICI|251109.change: Nov-2025: cautious ('soft quarter; bed addition critical to revive growth').
ICICI|251109.view: The lone sceptic, and although its timing was wrong (it pre-dated the beat), its core worry — that bed-addition execution is what makes or breaks the next leg — is exactly the right thing to watch. Don't dismiss the analyst just because one quarter went the other way.

ICICI|251107.change: Nov-2025: upgraded to Buy, PT ₹8,840; dated.
ICICI|251107.view: Superseded; useful only as a marker that the buy-side turned positive early.

ASK Automotive.summary:
Both covering houses are bullish on ASK Automotive, with no bear view on record. CLSA (May 2026, Outperform, PT ₹630) is the most current and substantive note; BP Wealth (Dec 2025, Buy, PT ₹593) is directionally aligned but now ~6 months stale. The PT cluster is tight at ₹593–₹630. CLSA's update highlights a ~2x revenue multiplier vs 2W industry volume growth in FY26 (23% revenue growth adjusted for the wheel assembly divestiture, vs 12% 2W production), suggesting sustained wallet-share and content gains at key OEMs. The real debate is whether this outperformance is durable into a more uncertain FY27, and whether the 4Q EBITDA margin dip (11.6%, down 138bps QoQ) marks the start of structural pressure or is a transient blip. Older Trendlyne entries from ICICI Securities (May 2024, TP ₹405) and JM Financial (Apr 2024, TP ₹375) are now over two years stale and not factored into the active thesis — they are noted for context on how far the stock has re-rated.

My own read: ASK Automotive's persistent revenue outperformance vs 2W volumes points to real content-per-vehicle gains — likely a combination of new product category additions and deepening share at key OEM relationships (the company's 2W focus means Hero/Honda/TVS concentration is a sword that cuts both ways). The EV lightweighting angle flagged by JM Financial in 2024 remains a credible structural tailwind, though 2W EV penetration is still modest and the timing of that uplift is uncertain. What I'd flag as under-discussed: the wheel assembly divestiture complicates the revenue comp and may flatter the "23% growth" narrative — stripping it out is the right methodology, but investors should verify how clean that adjustment is. The EBITDA margin trajectory at 11.6% and declining QoQ deserves closer scrutiny than the current coverage gives it; if OEMs are squeezing ASK's pricing as they manage their own cost lines, the premium multiple gets harder to justify. With only two active covering houses, both Buy, the stock is under-followed — which leaves more room for negative surprises to hit hard when they arrive. The 1–2 things I'd watch: FY27 margin guidance at the next results, and any OEM programme wins or losses in the new product pipeline.

CLSA|260520.change: PT maintained ₹630; Outperform maintained. No change vs prior report (prevTP ₹630 → currTP ₹630; prevCall OP → currCall OP).
CLSA|260520.view:
CLSA's May 2026 note is an FY26 results update, not a thesis-changing piece — it reinforces conviction without raising the target. The core bull case (content gains driving ~2x industry volume growth) is well-evidenced by the reported outturn, and the ₹630 PT held steady through a results season where the margin disappointed.

What I'd stress-test: the 4Q EBITDA margin dip to 11.6% (−138bps QoQ) gets brief treatment but is the most important variable. If CLSA is holding the PT flat despite a margin miss, their FY27 margin recovery assumption is doing significant work — and that assumption isn't validated in a results note. The report also predates any FY27 guidance disclosure. Credible and the anchor view, but the unchanged PT after a margin miss is a mild yellow flag rather than a clean green.

BPW|251201.change: Dated Dec-2025; no recent prior to compare. TP ₹593, Buy rating.
BPW|251201.view: BP Wealth's Dec 2025 note is now ~6 months old and predates CLSA's FY26 results update. At TP ₹593 it sits at a modest discount to CLSA's ₹630, directionally aligned. The headline — 'Shining Star Series BUY' — is a product-label screener note, suggesting a lighter initiation or screener-type write-up rather than a deep-dive thesis. Without the full text it is hard to independently assess the quality of the underlying analysis. I'd treat this as corroborating cover but not independent confirmation of CLSA's view; its staleness and probable lighter format mean it adds limited incremental information at this point.

AWL Agri Business.summary:
**JPMorgan** is the sole bear (UW, PT ₹190), viewing the Foods platform pivot as a long-dated, margin-uncertain story with the stock already priced for optimism. **Jefferies** (Buy, PT ₹260) is constructively positioned after the May 2026 analyst day, treating the ₹1tn-by-2030 sales target and mid-single-digit EO volume growth as credible anchors. **ICICI Securities** (Buy, PT ₹350, Nov-2025) is the most bullish but its note is ~7 months stale and the house actually trimmed its PT from ₹360 to ₹350 on the prior update — some caution crept in even before the analyst day. **Deven Choksey** (Hold, PT ₹274, Nov-2025) sits in the middle with a modest PT raise (₹265→₹274) but no upgrade conviction. The TP spread is wide — 1.37× from ₹190 (JPM) to ₹260 (Jefferies), with ICICI's ₹350 the outlier. The real debate centres on the **Foods margin trajectory**: JPMorgan flagged it as the key monitorable, seeing near-term margins largely stable; Jefferies is more optimistic about revenue-mix and scale benefits lifting margins.

My own read: AWL is the Fortune brand trying to escape the edible-oils trap, and the strategic logic is sound — Fortune's equity is genuine, the distribution reach is hard to replicate, and adjacencies like atta, ghee, and ready-to-cook are credible extensions. The problem is that roughly three-quarters of revenues will remain oil-price-sensitive for years, which means earnings volatility is structural, not transitional. ICICI's ₹350 target is hard to justify without a step-change in Foods gross margins that is not yet visible in the numbers. JPMorgan's UW at ₹190 at least reflects the near-term reality. I'd want two or three quarters of Foods margin expansion — not just revenue-mix shift — before warming to the bull case. The ₹1tn 2030 target is aspirational; hold it lightly. Key things to watch: quarterly Foods revenue share progression, Foods EBITDA margin per unit, and whether edible-oil profitability stabilises as the palm-oil cycle normalises.

JP|260526.change: PT unchanged at ₹190; UW maintained. pdfdata shows prevTP ₹190 → currTP ₹190, prevCall UW → currCall UW — stance reiterated in the analyst-day note with no change.
JP|260526.view:
JPMorgan is the sole Underweight and that contrarianism deserves weight. Their bear case rests on two pillars: (1) Foods margin improvement is real but slow — "largely stable near term" is their own language — so the rerating catalyst is years away; (2) at the ~₹193 CMP at time of writing versus a ₹190 PT, the stock was already priced for the transformation story without the execution proof.

The note was written from the same analyst-day event that Jefferies attended, yet the two came away with opposite conclusions — JPMorgan focused on what management did not say (Foods margin quantum, capex phasing, category-level profitability), Jefferies on the headline ₹1tn target. That divergence is instructive. A guided Foods volume share of ~25% over five years means the oil business stays dominant through FY30, and oil-business margins are structurally thin. The UW is the more disciplined call at current levels.

Jeff|260521.change: PT unchanged at ₹260; Buy maintained. pdfdata shows prevTP ₹260 → currTP ₹260, prevCall BUY → currCall BUY — stance reiterated at the analyst day with no revision.
Jeff|260521.view:
Jefferies' Buy is grounded in the analyst-day narrative: Foods platform build, Fortune brand leverage, ₹1tn-by-2030 aspiration, and a margin trajectory Jefferies themselves describe as "marginally better than JEFe" — meaning marginally ahead of their own prior model. The PT of ₹260 implies roughly 35% upside from the analyst-day CMP.

The bull case is coherent but execution-dependent. Fortune is a genuine branded moat and the distribution network is a real asset for category extensions. Where I'd push back: "marginally better than JEFe" on margins is not a strong enough incremental to justify a re-rating. The Foods business needs to demonstrate gross-margin expansion, not just revenue-mix shift, to validate the multiple. Until then, Jefferies' ₹260 PT sits at the optimistic end of a range that assumes a smoother transition than the operating history of this business would suggest.

DC|251110.change: PT raised ₹265→₹274 (trendlyne: prior entry 250717 Hold ₹265, current entry 251110 Hold ₹274); Hold maintained. No pdfdata match — trendlyne-sourced only.
DC|251110.view: Deven Choksey's Hold with a small PT bump to ₹274 reads as a cautious acknowledgment of sequential recovery without conviction on a re-rating. The headline "festive demand to drive H2 rebound" is standard seasonal commentary. This note predates the May 2026 analyst day and therefore does not reflect the Foods pivot strategy as laid out by management — it is effectively stale on the thesis level. The ₹274 PT sits well below both Jefferies and ICICI, suggesting Choksey was already discounting the long-term Foods story. Treat this as a low-conviction, pre-analyst-day view; the Hold is fair but offers little fresh insight.

ICICI|251106.change: PT trimmed ₹360→₹350 (trendlyne: prior entry 250716 Buy ₹360, current entry 251106 Buy ₹350); Buy maintained. No pdfdata match — trendlyne-sourced only.
ICICI|251106.view:
ICICI Securities holds the most aggressive PT at ₹350 — nearly double JPMorgan's ₹190 — a spread that warrants scrutiny. Their Nov-2025 Buy noted sequential recovery and foods-mix tailwinds, but even then the PT was trimmed from ₹360, signalling that the most bullish house was quietly pulling back. This note is ~7 months old and predates the analyst-day investor presentations.

At ₹350 ICICI is pricing in a Foods transformation that is not yet in the numbers. Their long history on this stock is instructive: they carried a Sell rating through 2023 (PT as high as ₹395) as earnings disappointed, then upgraded as volumes recovered. The pattern suggests the call is reactive to near-term momentum rather than a structural thesis. The directional trend of their own revisions — ₹395→₹375→₹360→₹350 — is a quiet de-rating story even from the most bullish house. I'd discount this target meaningfully.

Adani Enterprises.summary:
Only Jefferies covers Adani Enterprises in this library, and their current houseView (3 Jun 2026) is a conference day-1 takeaways note — not a standalone rated call. Their live Buy at ₹2,800 comes from the 2 Jun 2026 note, where both the TP and rating were held flat vs the prior report. There is no cross-house debate to map: no other broker is present in the library, and the 3 Jun note is descriptive rather than analytical, relaying panel themes around energy infrastructure and AI-driven power demand. The gap the library cannot fill is what the broader sell-side thinks — Jefferies' tone here is constructive but deliberately non-committal given the conference format.

My own read: AEL is best understood as a portfolio of early-to-mid-stage infrastructure incubations — airports, green hydrogen, roads, defense manufacturing, data centers — rather than a company with a clean, near-term earnings trajectory. The FY26 capex of ₹1.55tn is real and reflects genuine on-the-ground execution, but it also means the balance sheet is stretched and EBITDA visibility is limited across many sub-businesses. The post-Hindenburg stabilisation is real, but the group's USD debt load and reliance on ongoing capital market access remain structural vulnerabilities that the sell-side tends to underweight. The AI/power narrative sits more naturally with Adani Power and Adani Green than with AEL directly — AEL's edge is the incubation platform, not operating assets. Airports are the clearest near-term earnings driver; I'd watch concession EBITDA margins as greenfield capex ramps at newer airports. Fair value is genuinely hard to anchor: you are pricing optionality on India's infrastructure deficit with governance risk and conglomerate discount as the key unknowns. The stock rewards patience more than precision.

Jeff|260603.change: Conference takeaways note (3 Jun 2026); no TP or rating stated in this note. The latest rated Jefferies report (2 Jun 2026) maintained Buy at ₹2,800 — both TP and call unchanged vs their prior report (prevTP ₹2,800, prevCall Buy).
Jeff|260603.view:
The 3 Jun Jefferies note is a clean management-messaging recap from the Adani Group conference — useful for tracking what the group is emphasising (energy infra build-out, AI-led power demand, disciplined capex) but not a standalone investment thesis. The constructive framing is partly structural to the conference format, which naturally skews toward positives.

I'd treat the ₹2,800 Buy with measured scepticism: it is probably the right directional call if execution holds, but AEL's conglomerate structure makes that target harder to validate than a single-business stock — sum-of-the-parts analysis requires assumptions about listing timelines, holdco discounts, and capital recycling that can move the output substantially. The most useful thing to watch from Jefferies going forward: whether they update their airport EBITDA build (the clearest near-term earnings driver) and whether any report flags deterioration in holdco leverage metrics.

Adani Ports and SEZ.summary:
Coverage is overwhelmingly bullish — Jefferies, Nomura, Kotak, Motilal Oswal, and Prabhudas Lilladhar are all Buy/Add, with only **BOB Capital** recently downgraded to Hold. Price targets span ₹1,777 (PL, stale) to ₹2,160 (Jefferies), a wide spread. The credible live range is ₹1,820–₹2,160. **Jefferies** is the most aggressive bull at ₹2,160 (BUY, unchanged), anchoring the thesis on 1bnt cargo by 2030 and 100 bps/year RoCE expansion. **Kotak** and **Nomura** cluster near ₹1,900–₹1,930 and are broadly aligned. **Motilal Oswal** raised TP from ₹1,820→₹1,900 post the Q4FY26 beat. **BOB Capital** is the lone dissenter — downgraded from Buy to Hold and cut TP ₹1,960→₹1,820 in May 2026, citing a transient margin dip; their prior Buy note (Feb 2026) had been more optimistic than consensus. **PL** last covered in Aug 2025 at ₹1,777 — that target is below market and stale by ~10 months; effectively dead coverage. The real debate is (a) whether the Adani conglomerate risk-discount continues to narrow and (b) whether the heavy investment cycle compresses near-term EBITDA margins enough to matter — Jefferies says no, BOB says maybe.

My own read: ADSEZ is India's most defensible private port franchise — Mundra's scale is structurally irreplaceable and the integrated logistics build-out adds real earnings-quality upside over a 3–5 year horizon. Kotak's observation that capex is being funded 3x the historical pace from operating cash flow, not incremental debt, is the most encouraging data point in recent filings for an Adani entity. However, the stock is not obviously cheap at current levels: most live PTs (Kotak ₹1,900, Nomura ₹1,930, MO ₹1,900) sit within 5–7% of CMP, so the upside is Jefferies-scenario-dependent. The management-vs-JEF cargo CAGR gap (16% vs 13% to 2030) is material — at the JEF figure the valuation is disciplined; at management's figure it is generous. Two things I'd watch most: (1) whether the VLCC terminal at Mundra drives sustained liquid-cargo margin mix improvement through FY27, and (2) whether the 100 bps/year RoCE expansion target holds if the logistics segment's margin profile keeps diluting port EBITDA — that is the linchpin of the premium valuation.

Jeff|260604.change: PT ₹2,160 and BUY maintained — both unchanged from prior Jefferies report in library.
Jeff|260604.view:
Jefferies is the clear bull outlier at ₹2,160, roughly 14% above the Kotak/Nomura/MO cluster. Their conviction rests on two pillars: the 1bnt cargo target by 2030 (which they model at 13% CAGR vs. management's 16%) and a 100 bps/year RoCE expansion from FY26–31. The management-meet format means this note is directional, not a model update — so the unchanged TP is expected.

The Jefferies bull case is disciplined: they are already discounting management's volume aspirations by 3 pp of CAGR, not rubber-stamping them. I find the RoCE expansion target the more important watchpoint — if logistics dilutes group EBITDA margins, the RoCE trajectory stalls and the ₹2,160 target erodes. That said, Jefferies is the house with the deepest coverage history on ADSEZ and their 2030 framework is the most internally consistent of the bulls. Treat ₹2,160 as a blue-sky-execution scenario, not the base.

Kotak|260603.change: First Kotak report captured in the local library; no prior to compare. ADD at fair value ₹1,900.
Kotak|260603.view:
Kotak's ADD (rather than Buy) at ₹1,900 is the library's most conservatively framed bullish call — a subtle signal that they see fair value near current levels, not a meaningful rerating catalyst. The annual-report deep-dive is substantive: the finding that standalone investments/loans-and-advances ran at 3x the FY20–25 pace, funded from operating cash flow, is a genuine green flag for balance-sheet discipline in a conglomerate that has historically attracted leverage concerns.

I treat the Kotak ₹1,900 FV as the best available 'floor' fundamental valuation — any sustained trade above ₹1,900 implies the market is pricing in either the Jefferies blue-sky volume case or a further conglomerate discount compression, neither of which Kotak's base model captures. Worth noting: Kotak's ADD label means they would not be buyers at a significant premium to ₹1,900, which is a useful anchor.

Nomura|260602.change: PT ₹1,930 and BUY maintained — both unchanged from prior entry in pdfdata.
Nomura|260602.view:
Nomura's note is a monthly traffic update, not a thesis revision — and the unchanged TP reflects that. The 16% y-y volume growth in May 2026 with 15% YTD is operationally ahead of JEF's 13% CAGR model on an annualised basis, which is mildly positive for the bull case.

The detail worth flagging is the VLCC terminal ramp: liquid cargo up 33% y-y, supported by OMC customer wins. If that is a durable volume base (not a seasonal spike), it feeds a margin-mix tailwind that partially offsets any logistics dilution. Nomura's ₹1,930 sits in the consensus cluster; this note adds no new conviction but confirms the volume story is tracking.

BOB|260504.view:
BOB is the lone bear-adjacent voice and the downgrade is meaningful — they were at Buy with ₹1,960 as recently as February 2026, so this is not a perma-cautious stance but a genuine change triggered by Q4FY26 results. 'Margin dip transient' is hedged language: they are not saying the business is broken, but they are unwilling to pay up for a near-term margin wobble.

I'd discount the downgrade somewhat: BOB's ADSEZ coverage shows a pattern of reactive upgrades/downgrades around quarterly results (Buy after Q2FY26 beat, Hold after what appears a Q4FY26 margin miss). If Q1FY27 margins recover — especially if liquid cargo mix improves — BOB is likely to flip back quickly. The ₹1,820 Hold target is currently below consensus but not dramatically bearish; it is essentially saying 'wait for the margin recovery before buying.' That is a reasonable short-term stance, less useful as a structural view.

MO|260430.view:
Motilal's post-Q4FY26 raise is the cleanest data point in the trendlyne series — a 4.4% TP lift after a quarterly beat, reflecting confidence in the execution trajectory rather than a re-rating of the thesis. Their 'integrated transport utility company' framing is the right lens: they are capitalising ADSEZ's logistics overlay, not just port EBITDA multiples.

MO's ₹1,900 aligns with Kotak, which puts two independent consensus-calibre houses at the same level — that convergence is meaningful. The Jan 2026 note (TP ₹1,800, NQXT acquisition closure) suggests the TP upgrade path from ₹1,550 (May 2025) to ₹1,900 now has been a steady walk-up on improving visibility, not a step-change from a single catalyst. Credible and current; I'd treat MO's ₹1,900 as the base-case consensus.

PL|250805.change: Dated Aug-2025; only PL entry in library — no recent prior to compare. Buy at ₹1,777.
PL|250805.view: PL's note is a Q1FY26 result update from roughly 10 months ago — the ₹1,777 target is well below current market levels, meaning the stock has re-rated past PL's model without a fresh update. This is effectively stale coverage. The Buy rating is technically in place, but with no Q2/Q3/Q4FY26 follow-through, it carries no current informational weight. I would ignore this entry for positioning purposes and watch for a fresh note around Q1FY27 results (expected Jul/Aug 2026).

Sun Pharmaceuticals.summary:
The one genuinely split book here. **Bernstein** is the bull (Outperform, ₹2,235) on an under-appreciated US innovation franchise; **Kotak** is constructive (Add, raised to ₹1,960). Against them, **CLSA** (Hold, ₹2,020) and **Jefferies** are neutral, and **JPMorgan** is the bear, flagging a 4QFY26 EBITDA/PAT miss ~11-13% below consensus. The fault line is clean: optimism on the specialty re-rating versus caution on near-term earnings quality and US compliance/pricing. Tellingly, even the bulls disagree on magnitude — Kotak's ₹1,960 sits well below Bernstein's ₹2,235.

My own read: Sun's specialty pivot (Ilumya, Winlevi, Leqselvi, the SPARC NCEs) is the most credible branded-innovation transition in Indian pharma, and it genuinely lowers dependence on commoditised US generics — I buy the direction. The India branded franchise underneath is excellent: consistently growing ~2-3x the IPM, defensive and high-margin. Where I land closer to the bears: the swing factor for this stock has, for a decade, been **US FDA compliance at Halol** — and Halol/Baska are again pending reinspection. That single risk can gate the entire US franchise and is concrete in a way 'specialty is underappreciated' is not. I'd also discount the **GLP-1 / metabolic** ambition heavily — a crowded global field where Sun is a late, unproven entrant. So I weight JPMorgan/CLSA's caution slightly above Bernstein's optimism: own Sun for the India base plus specialty optionality, but size for the binary Halol risk and don't pay up for pipeline catalysts that haven't cleared the FDA. The Halol reinspection outcome is the thing to watch above all else.

Bern|260525.change: Maintained Outperform; PT held ₹2,235. Doubles down on the innovation arm as 'most underappreciated'.
Bern|260525.view: The most bullish and most thesis-driven take — and a useful articulation of the long-term case. But by construction it is talking up a re-rating that hasn't happened; 'most underappreciated' is a narrative, and the ₹2,235 print is the highest precisely because it front-loads pipeline success. Compelling if specialty delivers and Halol stays clean — two things not yet in hand.

CLSA|260524.change: Hold; PT ₹2,020. India/other regions offsetting tepid US generics.
CLSA|260524.view: A sensible fence-sitter — its 'strong India offsetting soft US generics' framing captures the real tension better than either extreme. Hold is an honest call here.

JP|260524.change: Bearish; flags 4QFY26 EBITDA/PAT ~11-13% below consensus on higher costs.
JP|260524.view: The most useful counterweight in the book. A double-digit EBITDA/PAT miss is concrete, not narrative — exactly the near-term earnings-quality signal the bull case tends to wave away. When the bears are pointing at reported numbers and the bulls at pipeline, the bears usually have the stronger near-term ground; I'd take this seriously.

Kotak|260524.change: Maintained Add; PT raised ₹1,850→₹1,960 despite muted Global Innovative Medicines sales.
Kotak|260524.view: Constructive but measured — and tellingly its raised PT (₹1,960) sits far below Bernstein's ₹2,235, which tells you even the optimists can't agree on how much the specialty arm is worth. That gap is itself evidence the re-rating is genuinely contested.

Jeff|260522.change: Neutral; broadly in-line quarter (India formulations solid).
Jeff|260522.view: Neutral, in-line quarter — adds to the cautious cluster. The real message of the book is that three of five houses are neutral-to-negative; the bull case is the minority view here, not the consensus.

Aegis Logistics.summary:
Only one house is represented in the local library: **JPMorgan** (OW, PT ₹1,010, June 2026), writing a First Take on 4QFY26 results. The trendlyne archive shows **Motilal Oswal** last at Neutral with PT ₹670 in May 2024 — two years stale and nearly 33% below JPMorgan's target — but that note predates the stock's significant re-rating and Aegis's capacity expansion cycle, so it cannot be treated as a live bear view. The local library has no active bear or neutral counterweight; JPMorgan is the only current voice, and its tone is unambiguously constructive after a large earnings beat.

My own read: Aegis runs a high-quality, asset-backed toll model — LPG and chemical terminal handling fees are structurally sticky, underpinned by long-term OMC agreements and India's rising LPG penetration in the eastern/rural pipeline. The 4QFY26 beat (adj PAT ₹4.1bn vs JPMorgan's ₹2.9bn estimate and street ₹2.4bn) was exceptionally wide, which is unusual for a terminal business with largely fixed contractual revenue — it signals either a non-recurring item in the gas division or that utilisation/throughput surprised sharply on the upside; the note does not clarify which, and that distinction matters for the sustainability of earnings. The two things I would watch most: (1) whether the gas-division beat was throughput-driven (durable) or a one-time revaluation/catch-up, and (2) the pace of Pipavav Phase III and Mumbai terminal capacity adds, which are the next leg of the growth story. At JPMorgan's ₹1,010 target the stock likely prices in a healthy expansion pipeline; any slip in commissioning timelines or OMC volume commitments would be the key de-rating risk.

JP|260601.change: PT maintained at ₹1,010; OW maintained (prevTP ₹1,010 → currTP ₹1,010; prevCall OW → currCall OW). This is a First Take note — no formal model revision, just results commentary.
JP|260601.view:
JPMorgan's comfort with OW and an unchanged ₹1,010 target despite a large earnings beat is telling: they were already well above street on their estimate (₹2.9bn vs ₹2.4bn), so the beat confirms rather than surprises their thesis. That suggests they have a differentiated, higher-conviction model on the gas terminal economics — worth weighting their view accordingly.

The caveat is that First Take notes are deliberately thin — no updated EPS, no revised terminal-value assumptions, no view on what drove the beat (throughput, tariff, or one-off). Until the full note lands with a model update, the ₹1,010 target should be read as a floor rather than a refined intrinsic-value estimate. I'd watch for their post-results detailed update to see if the target moves up materially, which would be the cleaner signal on where fair value sits post this earnings inflection.

Afcons Infrastructure.summary:
Nomura is the only house with an active Buy, carrying TP ₹417 (May 2026) while acknowledging a severe 4QFY26 miss — revenue down ~19% y-y — driven by the West Asia Crisis (WAC) disrupting overseas project execution. ICICI Securities sits at Hold, TP ₹420, but that note is from November 2025 and is now over seven months stale; it was already flagging order inflow quality before the WAC fully hit. The Jefferies filing (Jun 2026) is a broader India earnings review, not a company-specific call — no Afcons TP or rating is stated. The real debate is whether WAC disruptions are temporary (Nomura's bet) or whether the working-capital bleed and order-inflow lumpiness signal a more persistent drag (the implied ICICI concern). TP cluster of ₹417–₹420 is narrow given the divergence in conviction.

My own read: Afcons has a genuinely differentiated franchise — complex marine, underground and oil-and-gas EPC that most domestic peers cannot execute — and Shapoorji Pallonji's backing provides balance-sheet headroom and project-access advantages that the standalone financials undersell. That said, the WAC impact is not a simple timing issue: vendor advance-payment demands and material availability constraints alter working-capital dynamics in ways that can linger beyond the immediate disruption. A full recovery in FY27 is plausible but not guaranteed, and Nomura's TP appears to assume it. I'd be slightly more cautious than Nomura — the franchise is real but the near-term execution risk is under-discounted at current TP levels. The two things I'd watch most: (1) international order inflow replenishment in 1QFY27 — does Afcons replace the WAC-affected backlog at decent margins? (2) cash conversion and working-capital normalisation — if advance-payment terms persist, free-cash-flow generation will disappoint even if revenue recovers.

Jeff|260602.change: Dated Jun-2026; this is a broader India Mar-quarter earnings review note — no company-specific TP or rating for Afcons is stated in the report.
Jeff|260602.view: This Jefferies note offers no direct call on Afcons: it reviews broad market earnings trends (revenue +13%, PAT +15% for the market; downgrades rising on Middle East uncertainties; capital goods/construction flagged as slow). Its classification under Afcons likely reflects Afcons being part of Jefferies' coverage universe whose results were rolled into the note. The indirect signal is not flattering — Jefferies explicitly notes capital goods and construction lagging, and flags Middle East uncertainties as a source of downgrades. For a company with Afcons' West Asia exposure, that read-across is cautionary. Without a fresh standalone Afcons call from Jefferies in the library, this note adds no actionable TP or rating signal but contextually reinforces the WAC-related risk.

Nomura|260520.change: TP ₹417, Buy maintained; prevTP is absent from the library (this is the first captured Nomura report on Afcons — cannot confirm whether ₹417 represents a change vs an earlier Nomura report not in the library). Rating: Buy held.
Nomura|260520.view: Nomura's Buy is a through-the-cycle call: it acknowledges the 4QFY26 miss was bad (-19%/-12% y-y/q-q revenue, -19%/-23% vs estimates and consensus) but bets that WAC headwinds are temporary and the FY26–29 CAGR thesis remains intact. That's a reasonable structural view — Afcons' project mix and track record justify a premium over generic EPC peers. What I'd stress-test: TP ₹417 implies a full WAC recovery baked in, with little margin for another quarter of disruption. If 1QFY27 execution also disappoints (WAC uncertainty has not fully resolved as of Jun 2026), the model hits its limits fast. Nomura is right about the franchise; the question is whether FY27 is the inflection or the disappointment. I'd give this a conditional endorsement — credible if the recovery timeline holds, fragile if it slips.

ICICI|251114.change: Dated Nov-2025 (over 7 months ago); TP ₹420, Hold (Trendlyne). No newer ICICI report in the library. Note predates the worst of the WAC disruption that hit 4QFY26.
ICICI|251114.view: ICICI's Hold at TP ₹420 was prescient in flagging order inflow intensity as the key monitorable — that concern has only grown sharper since. The note was written after what ICICI called a 'subpar quarter', which in retrospect was a relatively mild warning shot before the 4QFY26 collapse. At 7+ months old, the TP and earnings assumptions are stale and likely no longer reflect management's own guidance. I'd treat ICICI's directional caution as still valid — Hold is probably the right posture — but the specific numbers need a refresh. Worth watching whether ICICI re-initiates coverage post the FY26 results and whether they nudge the TP down or revise the rating in light of WAC.

Alkem Laboratories.summary:
Five houses cover Alkem, split two bulls (Nomura, ICICI), two neutrals (JPMorgan, Motilal Oswal), one bear (BOB Capital). The freshest views are from 29 May 2026 post-4QFY26 results — JP, Nomura, and BOB. ICICI and MO are both from Feb 2026 and pre-date the 4Q print. Price targets span ₹4,638 (BOB Sell) to ₹6,890 (Nomura Buy), a ~49% gap that reflects genuine disagreement on FY27 margin trajectory. Nomura is the most constructive: the 11% EBITDA beat and 65.4% gross margin (+606bp YoY) vindicate their Buy; they acknowledge exceptional charges (₹1.35bn impairment + Labor Code) as one-offs. JPMorgan is measured — a modest TP nudge to ₹5,900 with Neutral maintained, flagging that higher gross margins were offset by elevated R&D and that margin visibility into FY27 remains limited. BOB is the outlier: a sharp downgrade from Hold to Sell with TP slashed from ₹5,962 to ₹4,638, arguing EBITDA margins are likely flat in FY27 and valuations are stretched. ICICI (Feb) framed India as a "temporary pause" with new-venture (CDMO/med-tech) scale-up ahead — that pause has partly resolved with 9% India growth in 4Q, but their ₹6,500 Buy hasn't been refreshed post-results. Motilal (Feb) focused on the Occlutech med-tech acquisition and stayed Neutral at ₹5,525, the most conservative among the non-bears.

My own read: Alkem's franchise in acute-care branded generics in India is one of the most durable in mid-tier domestic pharma — brand equity in antibiotics and GI is hard to replicate, and the 4Q gross margin expansion to 65.4% validates years of portfolio pruning away from low-margin US generics. That said, BOB's margin caution deserves more credit than the bull consensus gives it. R&D investment for CDMO ambitions is structural, not one-off, and Occlutech adds meaningful opex before it contributes meaningfully to earnings. At Nomura's ₹6,890 target, Alkem would trade at roughly 30–32x FY27E earnings — premium to mid-tier pharma peers and hard to justify unless India business reaccelerates well above 10% and CDMO/med-tech hits an inflection. I'd sit closer to JPMorgan's cautious neutral: the 4Q beat was real but the quality of FY27 earnings growth needs proof. Watch two things: (1) whether India branded generics sustain double-digit growth through H1FY27 (ICICI's "temporary pause" thesis needs ongoing validation); (2) whether Occlutech integration costs stay contained or creep into a drag. BOB's TP feels too punitive given the gross margin trajectory, but their core point on valuation is fair.

JP|260529.view:
JPMorgan's 4Q note is the most balanced of the three fresh views. They confirmed revenue broadly in line, EBITDA margin at 14.4% matching their estimate, and India sales up 9% YoY — a steady but unexciting outcome. The TP nudge of ₹100 is essentially a rounding adjustment rather than a conviction upgrade.

The key phrase in their title — "margin visibility limited" — is the honest read. Higher gross margins were offset by elevated R&D (CDMO build-out) and one-time costs (Labor Code, real estate impairment). JPMorgan's Neutral stance and below-consensus TP suggest they want to see FY27 guidance and execution before turning more positive. That's a credible, disciplined stance. Nothing in this note to argue with; the question is whether their margin estimates are conservative enough given continued CDMO opex ramp.

Nomura|260529.change: No prior Nomura report in the library to compare (prevCall not available); first captured report. PT ₹6,890; Buy.
Nomura|260529.view:
Nomura is the standout bull and the 11% EBITDA beat on gross margin expansion is the substantive hook for their case. A 65.4% gross margin (+606bp YoY, 420bp ahead of estimate) is a genuine positive — it signals pricing power and mix improvement in Indian branded generics.

However, Nomura appears to be treating the exceptional ₹1.35bn charge (real estate impairment + Labor Code) as cleanly one-off, which is partly right (the real estate piece probably is) and partly wrong (Labor Code impact may recur). Their TP at ₹6,890 is the highest in the coverage universe and prices in meaningful margin expansion. That's achievable in a benign scenario but leaves no margin of safety if R&D for CDMO or Occlutech integration costs run hot. The Buy is credible on the gross margin trajectory, but ₹6,890 is an optimistic scenario — treat it as an upside case, not a base.

BOB|260529.change: Downgraded Hold→Sell; PT slashed ₹5,962→₹4,638 (vs prior Hold at ₹5,962 on 15-Feb-2026 per trendlyne).
BOB|260529.view:
BOB's downgrade is the most aggressive move in this results round — a 22% TP cut and a rating flip to Sell. Their core thesis (EBITDA margins flat in FY27 on elevated opex; valuations expensive at current levels) is worth taking seriously even if the TP of ₹4,638 seems deeply pessimistic versus the rest of the pack.

BOB has historically been volatile on Alkem: Buy at ₹7,225 in Nov 2024, then Hold, then briefly Sell (Feb 2025 at ₹4,527), back to Hold, now Sell again. That oscillation suggests they're mark-to-market rather than structurally bearish — but the valuation point stands on its own merit. At ~30x+ FY27E, Alkem isn't cheap for a company with uncertain FY27 margin direction. I'd treat BOB as a useful contrarian signal on valuation and margin risk rather than a high-conviction structural short — but their argument that the gross margin beat doesn't automatically translate to EBITDA margin expansion (given R&D and CDMO opex) is the most useful single critique of the bull case.

ICICI|260215.view:
ICICI's February note framed the 3Q India slowdown as temporary and highlighted CDMO/new-venture scale-up as the medium-term catalyst. That narrative has partly played out — 4QFY26 India growth recovered to 9% YoY, partially validating the "pause" characterisation.

However, this note is now ~3.5 months old and pre-dates the 4QFY26 results. ICICI's ₹6,500 Buy is still directionally reasonable (in line with JP's revised view, below Nomura) but would benefit from a post-results refresh. The CDMO/Occlutech thesis is the longer-dated call — ICICI appears to be an early mover on that narrative. Worth revisiting when they update post-4Q; if they maintain Buy and raise TP, it would carry more weight.

MO|260214.view:
Motilal's February note on the Occlutech acquisition is the most thematic of the pre-results views — framing it as a med-tech diversification opportunity rather than an earnings catalyst. That's an honest characterisation: Occlutech (occlusion devices for structural heart disease) is a niche business that will take years to scale meaningfully in the Indian market.

MO's persistent Neutral and the lowest non-bear TP (₹5,525) reflects a "show me" stance: they want execution proof before turning constructive. The TP trimmed ₹35 in Feb is a signal they see near-term headwinds from opex rather than a catalyst. Post-4Q results, their TP looks conservative — the gross margin beat suggests the domestic business is in better shape than feared. MO may lag in upgrading. Their Neutral is credible but may be too cautious on the India franchise quality.

Amara Raja Energy and Mobility.summary:
Five houses cover Amara Raja, but the picture is split by vintage. The three current notes (all post-4QFY26 results, May 2026) are **Kotak** (Sell, TP ₹800), **JPMorgan** (Neutral, TP ₹925), and **Nomura** (Neutral, TP ₹942) — a tight cluster of bears and fence-sitters, with Kotak the clear outlier on the downside. The two older views — **Anand Rathi** (Hold, TP ₹1,490, Nov 2024) and **Geojit** (Buy, TP ₹1,682, Sep 2024) — are 18–21 months stale and should be set aside; they were written before the Gotion partnership collapse and reflect a new-energy optimism that has since been materially dented. The real debate among the current houses is whether the Gotion breakup is a fatal blow to the Giga corridor or a navigable setback. Kotak frames it as structural: removing the LFP technology pillar adds timeline and capex risk that the bull case cannot absorb. JPMorgan is more sanguine, pointing to accelerated BESS momentum (5 GWh by 4QFY27, NMC cell line on track for Jun-27) as an alternative engine. Nomura sits in the middle, flagging the margin miss (RM/sales +200bp q-q to 70.2%) as the near-term concern without taking a strong view on the new-energy pivot.

My own read: Amara Raja's lead-acid franchise — automotive OEM plus industrial — is genuinely underappreciated in all three current notes. It is a durable, cash-generative business, and the 16% revenue growth in 4QFY26 shows it is holding share. The new-energy story is the harder call. The Gotion break is a real setback: LFP chemistry was the chosen path for the Giga corridor, and pivoting mid-build to NMC (the cell line now being equipped) introduces both technology risk and the risk of competing against established global NMC players at a disadvantage. The 2024 re-rating that put sell-side TPs at ₹1,400–1,700 was premised on a clean LFP ramp that no longer exists. The neutral cluster at ₹925–942 looks fair given that uncertainty. I would not go as far as Kotak's Sell unless the BESS order pipeline also disappoints, but I would stress-test three things before turning constructive: (1) whether the Jun-27 NMC commissioning holds, (2) whether 5 GWh BESS capacity by 4QFY27 is supported by firm orders, and (3) whether the RM cost spike in 4QFY26 is transient or structural. Until those are clearer, this is a neutral-to-cautious hold rather than a re-rating opportunity.

Kotak|260527.view:
Kotak's bear case is the most internally consistent of the current pack. The EBITDA miss (1.5% below estimates despite a solid revenue beat) is a secondary concern — the primary issue is the Gotion partnership break, which Kotak reads as removing the LFP technology pillar of the Giga corridor and thereby adding material timeline and capex risk to the entire new-energy build-out. An unchanged TP at ₹800 signals conviction rather than recalibration.

This is the call worth engaging with most seriously. If the BESS/NMC path also slips — on equipment delays, cell yield issues, or a weaker-than-guided order pipeline — Kotak's ₹800 could prove generous. The Sell is a minority view among current brokers, but the reasoning is tighter than the neutral cluster's. Watch for updated capex guidance from management: any upward revision to the new-energy build cost would strengthen Kotak's case.

Nomura|260527.view:
Nomura's focus is granular and margin-driven. The 4QFY26 EBITDA miss traced entirely to RM/sales jumping 200bp q-q to 70.2% — a number that was above both Nomura's and Bloomberg consensus estimates. Revenue surprised the other way (7% beat), which makes the margin shortfall more notable: the business is growing but getting squeezed at the gross level.

The unchanged TP at ₹942 reflects a wait-and-see posture. The key question Nomura does not fully answer is whether the RM spike is a one-quarter inventory event (procurement timing, RM price volatility) or a structural shift in input costs. If transient, margins should recover and the Neutral stands. If structural, the Neutral risks being too generous. I would use Nomura's note primarily for the margin detail — the RM/sales trajectory is the cleanest near-term indicator of whether this business is tightening or loosening.

JP|260526.view:
JPMorgan is the most constructive of the three current houses, and also the most forward-looking. The TP raise reflects an upward revision in new-energy optionality: a credible 5GWh BESS target by 4QFY27, equipment already ordered for the 2GWh NMC cell line, and a management tone suggesting the Gotion gap is being actively filled rather than mourned.

The Neutral rating despite the constructive narrative is appropriate — there is a gap between management's accelerated push and what can be independently verified (order books, signed BESS contracts, cell yield targets). JPM's note provides the most useful pipeline detail of the three, and the BESS 10GWh roadmap is the figure I would track quarterly. If the 5GWh by 4QFY27 target is hit with firm customer commitments, the bull case starts to rebuild. If it slips or is customer-light, the TP raise looks premature.

AR|241107.change: Downgraded to Hold, TP ₹1,490 (Nov 2024). No prior Anand Rathi entry in the data to establish the exact prior TP; trendlyne confirms this was a downgrade event. Note is now ~19 months old.
AR|241107.view: This view predates the Gotion breakup by roughly 18 months and the 4QFY26 results by even longer. A TP of ₹1,490 reflects the new-energy optimism of late 2024, which has since been materially revised down by the rest of the sell-side. At current market levels and with the Gotion development now public, a ₹1,490 Hold target is effectively a stale Buy that hasn't been updated. Discount heavily; it adds little to current decision-making.

Geojit|240913.change: Upgraded to Buy, TP ₹1,682 (Sep 2024), up from Accumulate at TP ₹990 (Feb 2024) — a ~70% TP increase in 7 months. Note is now ~21 months old.
Geojit|240913.view: Geojit's Sep 2024 upgrade was a momentum call on the new-energy re-rating wave — a ₹1,682 target was aggressive even at the time and is now entirely disconnected from where sell-side consensus sits post-Gotion (₹800–942 range). The prior Accumulate at ₹990 in Feb 2024 shows how fast sentiment shifted in that period; the reverse has since occurred. Treat both Geojit entries as historical context only — neither figure is actionable, and neither reflects the current strategic picture.

Amber Enterprises.summary:
The three freshest notes (May–Jun 2026) all cut targets after a disappointing FY27 guidance call. **JPMorgan** (Neutral) took the hardest line, trimming PT to ₹7,650 and flagging two concrete PCB delays — Ascent Circuits trial pushed to Sep-Oct'26 and Korea Circuits trial now guided only by Q3FY28 (vs earlier 1HFY28) — plus revenue growth guidance well below consensus (Electronics 40% vs ~59% expected). **Kotak** held its Buy but clipped PT to ₹8,150, acknowledging a 17% PBT miss driven by higher D&A and interest. **CLSA** left its Outperform and ₹8,100 PT unchanged, using the note mainly to flag an unpriced catalyst: potential Oppo smartphone JV. The older bulls — **Anand Rathi** (₹10,050, Jul-2025) and **ICICI Direct** (₹9,500, Sep-2025) — are now ~10 and ~9 months stale respectively and their targets likely need revisiting post the FY27 guidance disappointment. **BOB Capital Markets** upgraded to Buy at ₹8,700 in Feb-2026 (from Hold at ₹7,740) on a Q3 rebound; that call too predates the May earnings miss. **ICICI Securities** (Hold, ₹7,000, Nov-2025) remains the most cautious named house, though its note on RAC weakness is also aging. The real debate is PCB execution timing vs. premium valuation: the bulls think delays are temporary; JP's Neutral reflects genuine doubt that the Electronics re-rating can sustain current multiples while commissioning slips.

My own read: Amber's RAC EMS franchise is one of the stronger moats in Indian manufacturing — scale, backward integration, and sticky OEM relationships make it structurally sound regardless of a given season's volume. But the market always ascribed a PCB/Electronics step-up premium to the stock, and consecutive delays erode credibility on exactly that thesis. The FY27 guidance cut (40% Electronics growth vs. 59% expected) is not a disaster, but it compounds with higher D&A and interest costs as the capex cycle bites before the revenue scales. Near-term margin is the honest story for FY27. The Oppo smartphone angle is the most interesting upside I see — if it moves to JV stage it opens a high-volume, secular vertical that current models don't carry — but I would treat it as call option, not base case. Key watches: Ascent Circuits first-production milestone (Sep-Oct'26 guidance), Electronics order book at Q1FY27 results, and whether a strong RAC summer restores operating leverage. At CMP ~₹7,154, the stock sits at a modest discount to the two fresh Bulls (Kotak ₹8,150 / CLSA ₹8,100); I would want a further 5–8% pullback before sizing up given the execution uncertainty.

CLSA|260521.change: PT unchanged ₹8,100; Outperform maintained. Catalyst watch note — no TP or rating move in this report vs prior.
CLSA|260521.view: CLSA's decision to hold the line while other houses cut is a deliberate choice: they are reserving a separate upgrade event for if/when the Oppo smartphone JV is confirmed, rather than baking it in now. That discipline is reasonable — the JV remains speculative newsflow, not a signed contract. The implication is that CLSA's ₹8,100 carries no JV premium yet, which makes their Outperform incrementally more interesting as a risk/reward if the JV progresses. What I would watch: any formal Oppo announcement is a genuine re-rating trigger since smartphone EMS volumes would dwarf RAC; conversely, if the JV talks go quiet, CLSA's unchanged PT starts to look like inertia rather than a considered hold.

JP|260518.change: PT cut ₹8,500→₹7,650; Neutral maintained. Post-earnings call note flagging below-consensus FY27 revenue guidance and concrete PCB commissioning delays.
JP|260518.view:
JP's is the most analytically grounded note of the May batch. The three takeaways — guidance miss, Ascent Circuits delay, Korea Circuits construction start — are all verifiable execution signals, not sentiment. The PCB delay matters more than the near-term margin squeeze: it is the pivot on which the entire re-rating thesis rests, and moving Korea Circuits trial from 1HFY28 to Q3FY28 is the second slip on that project. JP's ₹7,650 PT is the lowest of the current-month set; at CMP ~₹7,154 it implies only ~7% upside on a Neutral, which is a politely cautious way of saying 'not yet.'

I find JP's stance credible and would not dismiss it as reflexively conservative. If the Ascent Circuits Sep-Oct timeline also slips at Q1FY27 results, JP's Neutral could drift toward an underperform posture. The stock needs a clean execution print — not just volume, but margin normalisation and a PCB commissioning update — to shake the neutral camp loose.

Kotak|260518.change: PT cut ₹8,500→₹8,150; Buy maintained. PBT 17% below estimates — EBITDA in-line but higher D&A and interest costs weighed. PCB commissioning timing flagged as key risk.
Kotak|260518.view:
Kotak's trim-but-hold is the most pragmatic read in the set: acknowledge the miss, lower the PT modestly, retain conviction on the thesis. The logic is defensible — EBITDA was in-line, so operating performance was not the problem; the margin miss was financial leverage from the PCB capex cycle. That is a 'later not never' situation as long as PCB commissions on schedule.

The risk to Kotak's Buy is a further timeline slip. Their ₹8,150 Fair Value already factors in the current delay; a second slip to Ascent Circuits or Korea Circuits would force a more meaningful cut and possibly a rating review. Kotak's buy case is essentially a call option on PCB execution — I agree with the direction but the upside/risk is asymmetric enough that I would want more margin of safety than the current ~14% implied upside from ₹7,154.

BOB|260210.change: Upgraded to Buy (was Hold at TP ₹7,740 per Jul-2025 trendlyne entry); PT raised ₹7,740→₹8,700. Q3FY26 rebound and Electronics momentum cited. Note is ~4 months old, pre-dates the May-2026 earnings miss.
BOB|260210.view: BOB's February upgrade caught a genuine Q3 rebound well, but the May-2026 earnings call and PCB delay disclosures have materially changed the information set since then. Their ₹8,700 PT was the most aggressive of the post-Q3 cohort; it now looks stretched vs the ₹7,650–₹8,150 range from the May-2026 fresh notes. I would expect BOB to revisit post Q4 results — if they maintained Buy through the May earnings miss without a note update, the rating is technically stale. Worth watching their next publication to see if the upgrade conviction holds.

ICICI|251109.change: Upgraded from Sell to Hold (was Sell at TP ₹5,625 per Oct-2024 trendlyne entry); PT raised to ₹7,000. Noted RAC weakness and expected deleveraging benefits from H2FY26. Dated Nov-2025 — now ~7 months old.
ICICI|251109.view: ICICI Securities (the institutional research arm) was the last remaining bear in the institutional set — a Sell at ₹5,625 as recently as Oct-2024 — and moved to Hold only after the stock re-rated significantly. The ₹7,000 Hold TP is the most cautious current target and is now ~2% below CMP, implying a mild overvalued view. That caution was somewhat vindicated by the May-2026 earnings miss. However, the note is aging; ICICI's H2FY26 deleveraging thesis may or may not have played out by now. The honest read: ICICI was right to be cautious earlier; their Hold at ₹7,000 is a fair anchor for the bear case, but the note needs refreshing post the FY27 guidance call.

ICICI|250908.change: Upgraded to Buy with TP ₹9,500 (per trendlyne headline; the note explicitly states an upgrade). No prior ICICI Direct entry in the data to compare formally. Dated Sep-2025 — now ~9 months old.
ICICI|250908.view: ICICI Direct's ₹9,500 Buy from Sep-2025 was the most aggressive target in the history available and was likely written in a period of stronger sentiment about the PCB scale-up. Nine months on, the stock trades ~25% below that target and the FY27 guidance has disappointed. The call is factually stale. I would discount this view heavily until ICICI Direct publishes a post-FY27-guidance update — the original thesis about PCB-driven re-rating has not been invalidated but the timeline has clearly stretched.

AR|250731.change: Buy retained at TP ₹10,050 (per trendlyne). No prior Anand Rathi entry in the data. Dated Jul-2025 — now ~10 months old.
AR|250731.view: Anand Rathi's ₹10,050 was the highest target in the library and at ~40% premium to CMP today it is the most stale view in the set. The note referenced strong quarterly performance and acquisitions scaling industrial EMS — the thesis directionally remains intact but the valuation anchoring has shifted meaningfully after PCB delay disclosures and FY27 guidance cuts. I would treat AR's target as a bull-case ceiling from a prior information set, not a current live call. An AR update post the May-2026 earnings call would be the first useful signal from them in over three quarters.

Anthem Biosciences.summary:
All three houses covering Anthem Biosciences are bullish with no bears in sight. Targets cluster at ₹850–₹900: Nomura and BOB Capital both at ₹900, JPMorgan at ₹850 (just raised from ₹790 in May 2026). The 4QFY26 result — record revenues, EBITDA margin of 44% (+324bp YoY, 209bp above Nomura's estimate), CRDMO segment +31% YoY and +54% QoQ — was the catalyst that put post-3Q destocking concerns to rest. No house upgraded post-results (all were already Buy/OW); BOB raised its TP from the ₹835 initiation level to ₹900. JPMorgan provides the deepest forward framing, citing 10 Phase III molecules, 14 commercial assets, and 100+ early-stage projects. The real debate going forward is pace of CRDMO pipeline conversion and whether 44% EBITDA margins are structurally repeatable — not bull-vs-bear.

My own read: Anthem is a genuinely differentiated small-cap CRDMO story with margin quality that is extraordinary for its scale — 44% EBITDA at this revenue base reflects both pricing power in niche fermentation/biologics synthesis and tight cost control. Sell-side unanimity is itself worth questioning: with no bear on the register, the stock may be priced for near-perfection. I'd watch three things: (1) Phase III→commercial conversion over the next 4–6 quarters — a clinical failure in one or two key molecules could disproportionately hit revenue; (2) specialty ingredients deceleration (8% YoY vs CRDMO at 31%) — if this segment stagnates, overall growth becomes more concentrated and lumpy; (3) capex execution and whether backward integration delivers the margin protection JPMorgan expects without balance-sheet strain. Compared to the houses, I'd be constructive but would want two consecutive quarters of strong CRDMO commercial revenue before treating ₹900+ targets as conservative.

Nomura|260521.view:
Nomura's note is precise and data-grounded — they called the 4QFY26 recovery "in line with expectations" after flagging the 3Q weakness, which lends their stance credibility (they were neither caught off-guard by the dip nor surprised by the bounce). The 44% EBITDA margin beat (+209bp above their own estimate) is the headline number; they flag CRDMO +31% YoY as confirmation the growth engine has normalised post-destocking.

I'd give this note solid weight: holding TP flat at ₹900 despite the margin beat signals disciplined forecasting rather than earnings-driven exuberance. The main thing I'd probe from Nomura's vantage is specialty ingredients — 8% YoY is modest, and if CRDMO ever hits another lumpy quarter, that segment offers limited cushion.

BOB|260521.change: TP raised ₹835→₹900 vs the Feb-2026 initiation; Buy maintained (no pdfdata match for this note; prior TP sourced from Trendlyne initiation entry dated 260227).
BOB|260521.view:
BOB Capital Markets initiated on Anthem in Feb 2026 with a "full-spectrum CRDMO capabilities" thesis at ₹835; the May 2026 update lifts the target to ₹900, matching Nomura, framed as "growth drivers intact, industry-leading margins to sustain." The update note is thin on new analytical substance — it reads as affirmation rather than differentiated insight.

BOB is a smaller domestic broker; I'd treat the ₹900 TP as tracking consensus rather than independently derived. The value of this note is primarily as a confirmation data point that the domestic broker community has fully bought the margin-quality story — useful for sentiment, not for incremental edge.

JP|260520.view:
JPMorgan's note is the most analytically substantive of the three. They articulate three specific FY27 catalysts: destocking normalisation in select CRDMO molecules, backward integration driving structurally higher gross margins, and pipeline deepening (10 Phase III, 14 commercial assets with four in early ramp-up, 100+ early-stage projects). Their same-day First Take confirmed the clean in-line/beat print before the detailed thesis fleshed out the multi-year frame.

Two things to stress-test: JP's TP of ₹850 is the most conservative of the three — either they're appropriately cautious on specialty-ingredients growth or they're embedding some execution discount on the capacity expansion capex. The backward-integration margin thesis is compelling but timeline- and cost-dependent; I'd track RM cost savings against capex outflows each quarter. On balance, JPMorgan's note offers the most useful forward framework — their pipeline-depth metrics (Phase III count, commercial ramp-up cadence) are the primary scorecard I'd track over the next two quarters.

Apar Industries.summary:
Two houses cover Apar Industries post Q4FY26 results, and they split on the call: **Nomura** stays Buy (TP ₹14,240, unchanged) while **PL** has downgraded from Accumulate to Hold (new TP ₹13,309). Notably, PL's own TP rose ~38% in this same note (from ₹9,629 at the March 2026 management-meet update), which means both houses agree the business is executing strongly — the disagreement is purely on whether the stock still offers enough upside at current levels. Nomura raised its FY27F–FY28F EBITDA estimates 7–9% after the beat and projects a FY26–29F EBITDA CAGR of 19%; Q4FY26 revenue grew 27% y-y and EBITDA came in 3–5% above estimates. The targets are closely clustered (₹13,309–₹14,240), so the bull/hold divide is thin — a valuation call, not a thesis disagreement.

My own read: Apar is a high-quality compounder inside India's multi-year T&D build-out — conductors, cables, and transformer oil all benefit from PGCIL capex, state-distribution upgrades, and fast-growing export demand (US/EU grid investment). The Q4FY26 beat and Nomura's estimate upgrades confirm the business is delivering, not just riding a sector narrative. PL's repeated cycle of downgrading-then-chasing (from Buy in 2022 → Accumulate → Hold, while the TP kept rising) is a pattern worth noting — their caution has consistently underestimated the stock. That said, the Hold call is reasonable as a valuation discipline at elevated multiples. The risks I would watch most: (1) export-cable book concentration and whether US tariff/trade dynamics introduce margin risk; (2) aluminium and copper cost cycles — raw-material tailwinds flattered FY26 margins and could reverse; (3) the ₹15bn FY27E capex guidance — at this scale, execution slippage or demand softening could compress the multiple quickly. For a long-term holder the story remains intact; for a new entry, waiting for a valuation reset would be prudent.

PL|260529.change: PT raised ₹9,629→₹13,309 (from trendlyne prior entry dated 260316, Accumulate); rating downgraded Accumulate→Hold. No pdfdata entry for this note — change derived from trendlyne sequence.
PL|260529.view:
PL's downgrade is a valuation call, not a business signal — they are raising the PT nearly 38% in the very note they cut to Hold. The headline 'Strong T&D tailwinds anchor long term outlook' paired with a Hold is a classic 'great company, full price' message, and the market has likely priced in much of the medium-term upside.

I would treat this with some scepticism about the permanence of the Hold: PL's track record on Apar has been persistently too cautious across multiple cycles (Buy in Nov-2022 at ₹1,834, then a string of Accumulate/Hold cuts as the stock kept compounding toward ₹13,000+). Their TP of ₹13,309 could again prove conservative if the order pipeline stays robust and export execution continues to beat. Still, flagging valuation risk after a large re-rating is fair discipline, and the margin-of-safety at current levels is thin.

Nomura|260528.change: PT unchanged at ₹14,240; Buy maintained. EBITDA estimates raised 7–9% for FY27F–FY28F following Q4FY26 beat.
Nomura|260528.view:
Nomura's post-results note is substantive and estimate-driven rather than narrative: a 3–5% EBITDA beat, 27% revenue growth y-y, and a meaningful upward revision to two-year forecasts justify the maintained Buy without needing to stretch the story. The FY26–29F EBITDA CAGR of 19% is ambitious but grounded in the Q4 delivery.

The unchanged TP (₹14,240) alongside estimate upgrades is slightly puzzling — if EBITDA goes up 7–9% but the TP doesn't move, Nomura is implicitly compressing the target multiple, which is a quiet acknowledgment that valuation risk is rising even for the bull case. Worth watching: the ₹15bn FY27E capex guidance is large for Apar's historical scale; if domestic T&D order inflows slow or the export book faces margin pressure, that capex commitment could become a leverage risk rather than a growth driver.

Ashok Leyland.summary:
Five houses cover Ashok Leyland post Q4FY26 results, and the spread is notable. **Kotak** is the bear (Reduce, PT ₹170, cut from ₹190) — it sees a CV cycle peaking under diesel-price pressure and deteriorating fleet-operator profitability. **JPMorgan** and **BOB Capital** are neutral (Neutral/Hold, PTs ₹175 and ₹186 respectively), both citing muted near-term volume growth and cost inflation headwinds. **CLSA** is the quiet constructive voice (Outperform, PT ₹183) though it's the first report in our library — no prior delta to compare. **Motilal Oswal** formally holds a Buy (PT ₹185) but that note is from early April, pre-Q4 results, and carries a large prior TP cut (₹238→₹185); its optimism deserves a haircut. **Deven Choksey** (Accumulate, TP ₹156, Nov 2025) is the most stale and effectively a pre-cycle-peak view. Real debate: is the soft patch a 1–2 quarter digestion or the start of a prolonged CV downturn? Kotak says the latter; JPMorgan's focus on pricing discipline suggests it's manageable. Targets cluster ₹170–186, close to current levels — the market itself is pricing in little upside.

**My own read:** I'd sit closer to neutral-cautious than the bulls. Ashok Leyland had a genuine multi-year earnings recovery from the FY20–22 trough, but several factors now work against re-rating: diesel prices rising mid-cycle, global freight softness filtering into domestic operator sentiment, and Tata Motors defending share aggressively. The pricing discipline that both AL and Tata have maintained through FY26 is the most important positive — if that holds, margins won't collapse even if volumes disappoint. But I'm sceptical about volume growth assumptions for FY27: fleet operators absorbing a diesel hike while freight rates are sticky will crimp replacement demand. Defence and LCV exposure add structural support at the margin, but neither is large enough to offset a MHCV slowdown. The two things I'd watch: monthly wholesale dispatch trends through June–August (before the festive push), and whether fleet utilisation data from logistics players shows any stabilisation. Below ₹155–160 the risk/reward gets more interesting; at current levels (mid-₹160s), the Kotak Reduce is hard to dismiss.

Kotak|260529.view:
Kotak's bear case is built on macro rather than company-specific failure: diesel prices up mid-cycle, geopolitical tensions sustaining input cost volatility, and fleet operators' profitability getting squeezed before they can pass costs on. The PT cut from ₹190 to ₹170 is a meaningful 11% markdown reflecting downward earnings revision, not just de-rating.

I find this the most credible current call. The bear isn't saying AL is a structurally broken business — it's saying the cyclical tailwind has turned to a headwind and consensus earnings estimates are still too high for FY27. The Reduce with a PT still above current price signals limited near-term upside rather than a catastrophic sell — but in a soft-cycle environment, a Reduce from a fundamental house like Kotak tends to anchor sentiment for the quarter.

BOB|260529.change: TP cut ₹199→₹186 (vs Feb-2026 report); Hold maintained.
BOB|260529.view:
BOB has been on a steady downgrade path — it downgraded to Hold in February (from a prior Buy) at ₹199, and now cuts further to ₹186. The headline 'Steady Q4; muted growth, cost inflation to impact show' is accurate but uninspiring. Three consecutive downward TP moves from a house that was more constructive earlier in the cycle is a meaningful signal: the easy money in Ashok Leyland has been made.

The Hold at ₹186 with current price mid-₹160s does imply ~14% upside on paper, but I'd treat BOB's target as a ceiling in a flat cycle rather than a base case. Not a sell trigger, but not a reason to add.

JP|260528.view:
JPMorgan's modest PT lift to ₹175 is the most nuanced read: they acknowledge the Q4 miss (EBITDA 2% below JPMe) but emphasise 'pricing discipline likely to continue amid volatile demand.' That's the key bull embedded in a neutral stance — if Ashok Leyland and Tata hold the line on pricing, EBITDA margins stay resilient even on softer volumes.

I respect the pricing-discipline argument but would stress-test it: it holds so long as utilisation stays above ~80% for fleets. If utilisation dips meaningfully (say, festive season disappoints or exports slow), the pricing truce between AL and Tata can fray fast. JPMorgan's Neutral is intellectually honest — neither a screaming buy nor a sell — but the asymmetry of risks at current cycle positioning makes me lean toward Kotak's view.

MO|260401.change: TP cut sharply ₹238→₹185 (vs Feb-2026 report); Buy maintained.
MO|260401.view:
Motilal Oswal's April note already flagged 'CV outlook at risk if global headwinds persist longer' — which turned out prescient given the subsequent diesel-price increase. But the note is now over two months old and pre-dates Q4FY26 results; the Buy at ₹185 should be treated as stale. More telling: MO had already slashed the PT from ₹238 to ₹185 (a 22% cut) in response to macro deterioration.

MO remains structurally bullish on the CV cycle's medium-term recovery thesis, but their near-term caution is evident in the large TP cut. I'd want to see their post-Q4 update before giving this Buy weight — the current view may have been revised even more cautiously after results.

DC|251119.change: Rating downgraded Buy→Accumulate; TP marginally raised ₹155→₹156 (vs Aug-2025 report).
DC|251119.view:
Deven Choksey's November 2025 note is effectively pre-cycle-peak and now 7 months stale — the 'robust operational quarter' it celebrated was Q2FY26, well before the diesel price shock and the FY27 demand moderation concerns.
